reflections.title: Guarding Our Hearts from Worldly Compromise

reflect.text: King Jehoshaphat was a good king who sought God, but he made a dangerous compromise. Even though he had great wealth and honor, he formed an alliance with King Ahab, who hated the Lord. Jehoshaphat ignored a true prophet's warning and joined a disastrous battle. God graciously protected him and brought him safely home, but He sent the prophet Jehu to confront him. Helping those who oppose God and acting like them is a serious wrong against the Lord.

We can also fall into the trap of trying to see how close we can get to the world without getting hurt. As F. B. Meyer observed, "Love to the Lord Jesus is our only safeguard." When our hearts are truly attached to Christ, we no longer want to copy worldly ways. God balances His justice with deep compassion. Even while He lovingly corrects us for compromise, He sees our repentant hearts and remembers the good we have done in seeking Him.

questions: In what areas of your life might you be blending in too closely with worldly ways?
How can growing in your love for Jesus protect your heart from making ungodly compromises?
reflections.prayer: Lord, help us to keep our hearts completely devoted to You. Forgive us for the times we compromise and try to blend in with the world. Draw us closer to Jesus, so that our love for Him guides all our choices and friendships. Amen.
